slot.brief: Dehydrohalogenation of a given alkyl halide with alc. KOH; ask major Saytzeff vs Hofmann product.

stem: The major product formed when 2-bromo-3-methylbutane is heated with alcoholic KOH is:

verdicts.working: Alcoholic KOH promotes β-elimination. Removing a β-hydrogen from C3 forms the more substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, which is the major product by Zaitsev’s rule.

working:
E2 elimination with alc. KOH follows Saytzeff rule. Substrate has β-hydrogens at C-1 (primary) and C-3 (tertiary). Elimination from C-3 gives the more substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, as the major product.

Independent check: Alcoholic KOH promotes β-elimination. Removing a β-hydrogen from C3 forms the more substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, which is the major product by Zaitsev’s rule.
solution:
Alcoholic KOH promotes E2 elimination; by Saytzeff’s rule, the more substituted alkene is the major product.
$$\text{2-bromo-3-methylbutane} \xrightarrow[-\mathrm{HBr}]{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{2-methylbut-2-ene}$$
